content:
Lean's olean mechanism involves writing a preferred address into the header of the olean file. The preferred address is allocated here. When reading olean files, the strategy is:

  • Try to mmap all the files at their requested addresses. If this succeeds, great!
  • Otherwise, clean up and read all the files into one very big allocation (with mostly unused pages).

While this certainly works for building parts of lean itself, I'm finding (with a patched and strangely-built copy of lean) that once things get into mathlib, the addresses clash and everything takes the slow path; especially if using a downstream file that is not using the module system.

Should there be a metric on radar which is "number of lean invocations which successfully mmap", so that there is some way of telling when the mmaping is dead?
Ah it looks like I misunderstood the scope of the mapping; "all the files" is just the 4 pieces of the olean, not the ~20k pieces from all of mathlib.
I was completely unaware of that and docs#Lean.Environment.displayStats, thanks!
